items.acceptance_evidence: Fix commit f7de0c71b9 (2026-06-17) normalizes Date values to ISO date strings before the comparison, and commit a386a72991 (same day) adds integration tests pinning that an unchanged resent date no longer emits an update event.
items.description: The changed-field detection compares each incoming DTO value against a map built from the serialized entity, but the entity types its seven date fields as Date objects while the update DTO types them as ISO date strings — so the inequality is always true for any non-null date field. A PATCH that re-sends an unchanged deadline (forms commonly resend all fields) reports that field as changed and publishes a case-updated event though nothing changed: a phantom event for every consumer and an unreliable changed-fields list, violating the repo's authored domain-events rule that events fire only on real state change. Values must be normalized to a common representation before comparing.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fix commit f7de0c71b9 (2026-06-17) adds the transactional decorator to the method.
items.description: The task-graph creation method publishes domain events but carries no transactional decorator of its own. All four current callers are transactional, so the publish rides the caller's transaction via required propagation — but the first future non-transactional caller hits a runtime enqueue-outside-transaction error, and unit tests with a mocked bus will not catch it. Decorate the method defensively so the publish is always inside a transaction.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fix commit f7de0c71b9 (2026-06-17) adds the transactional decorator to the create method.
items.description: The assignment-creation method publishes an assignment-created domain event but is not itself transactional; it is safe only because its sole current caller is transactional. The same fragility as the task-graph path: a future non-transactional caller fails at runtime rather than at compile or test time. Decorate the method to match the team convention of publishing inside a transaction.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fix commit f7de0c71b9 (2026-06-17) adds a code comment documenting the asymmetry as intentional (bulk template hydration, not a user-driven assignment action) and pointing consumers at the task-created event instead.
items.description: Provisioned tasks emit a created event per task, but their assignments are inserted in bulk by the repository layer, bypassing the assignment service — so provisioned assignments never emit assignment-created events while custom-task assignments do. Any downstream consumer wanting the full assignment lifecycle sees only a subset. The asymmetry needed an explicit intentional-or-gap decision; the author resolved it by documenting it as intentional in the code.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fix commit f7de0c71b9 (2026-06-17) deletes the method.
items.description: A repository method that finds non-terminal assignments for a task has no callers anywhere — it is a leftover of a pre-read approach that was replaced by having the batch-cancel query return the actually-cancelled rows. Dead code added and orphaned within the same change; remove it.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fix commit f7de0c71b9 (2026-06-17) renames the constant key and its usages.
items.description: The event constant is keyed with a custom-created name although it is published for both custom and provisioned task sources — the prefix misleads consumers into assuming it covers only user-created tasks. The string value is fine; rename the constant key to the unqualified created form.
